question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what probe movement is being performed at the beginning of the exam, and what is the main imaging objective?
A. Rock (heel-toe) the probe in place to reduce anisotropy and better delineate the myotendinous junction without translating along the limb.
B. Maintain a cross-sectional view while sliding proximally to track the target muscle toward its proximal attachment
C. Rotate the probe into a longitudinal plane to obtain a long-axis view for assessment of fiber and tendon continuity.
D. Sweep side-to-side in short axis to screen the muscle belly for a focal tear or hematoma rather than following it proximally to its attachment.
groundtruth: The operator identifies the rectus femoris in transverse (short-axis) and then tracks it proximally toward the hip/AIIS region, noting the muscle cross-section progressively narrows as the scan approaches the proximal attachment.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the video clip, what stage of the workflow is being shown across this segment, and what is the next logical step?
A. Establishing the primary bony reference landmark first; next, sweep proximally and distally from that landmark to map the course of the target structure.
B. Initial localization and distal tracking; next, apply color Doppler to distinguish the structure from adjacent vessels before continuing the sweep.
C. Initial localization and proximal tracking; next, stabilize at the proximal attachment to identify key reference landmarks
D. Image optimization and confirmation of depth/orientation; next, obtain static measurements (e.g., cross-sectional area or thickness) at the point of maximal clarity.
groundtruth: The operator first localizes the rectus femoris in transverse view and tracks it proximally until it becomes tendinous. The workflow then proceeds to holding at the proximal attachment to identify nearby bony/joint landmarks before detailed insertion interrogation.

question:

A. Heel-toe (rock) the probe to keep the ultrasound beam perpendicular to the tendon/enthesis and reduce anisotropy.
B. Translate the probe side-to-side across the attachment to survey the full footprint/origin
C. Rotate the probe into the orthogonal (short-axis) plane to confirm the attachment margins and differentiate tendon from adjacent structures.
D. Fan/tilt the probe through the attachment to interrogate for focal partial-thickness tearing or calcific enthesopathy.
groundtruth: The operator slides the transducer from medial to lateral across the insertion point to visualize the full tendon origin at the inferior iliac spine region.
